latest_news.headline: Sarmada weapons-depot explosion: Syrian authorities report 14 dead in preliminary toll
latest_news.text: SANA reports a September 9 explosion at a weapons depot in Burj Elnumra near Sarmada, citing local health and emergency officials. Its earlier toll was three killed and ten injured. DW, credited with AFP, AP and Reuters, reports the Idlib health department’s preliminary toll of 14 killed and 11 injured and says the cause has not been announced. These are attributed, evolving counts rather than independent casualty verification. This is distinct from the September 1 Binnish ammunition-vehicle explosion.
sources: DW with AFP, AP, Reuters citing Idlib health department
latest_news.originating_source: Idlib Health Directorate and emergency official via SANA
latest_news.implication: Secondary explosions and fires hampered rescue efforts; the cause remains unannounced, so this is not established as a new attack.

latest_news.headline: Jordan reports intercepting 18 of 20 Iranian missiles; no casualties reported
latest_news.text: Petra carries the JAF statement that air defences engaged 20 ballistic missiles from Iranian territory, intercepting 18; two fell in unpopulated areas and no casualties were recorded. Reuters attributes an Al Azraq base attack to the IRGC and reports a US official described strikes as ineffective. Iranian heavy-damage claims are not independently verified. Counts and outcomes remain attributed. This September 9 attack is distinct from earlier Larak-related attacks and the September 8 US tanker strikes.
sources: Reuters citing Jordan, Iran and a US official
BBC citing JAF; not independent count verification
latest_news.originating_source: Jordan Armed Forces statement via Petra
latest_news.implication: The reported Iranian missile attack extends the latest US-Iran exchange to Jordan; interception and casualty figures remain attributed to Jordanian authorities.

latest_news.headline: CENTCOM reports five Iranian tankers struck on September 8
latest_news.text: CENTCOM states it struck Kaviz, Charminar, Horizon 1 and Riesco in the Gulf of Oman and Derya near Kharg Island on September 8, after attempted missile attacks on a US warship. It says crews were ordered to abandon ship and vessels rendered inoperable. Reuters reports the same US statement; this is not independent verification of the damage. This is distinct from the three tankers struck on September 5.
sources: Reuters citing CENTCOM (not independent damage verification)
latest_news.originating_source: U.S. Central Command Public Affairs via DVIDS
latest_news.implication: The US military reports additional strikes on Iranian oil shipping, distinct from its September 5 operation; damage remains attributed.

latest_news.headline: Saudi authorities report 73 civilians injured in Houthi attacks on four southern cities
latest_news.text: Petra carries the Saudi statement reporting 73 civilians injured in Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jazan and Najran on September 8. Anadolu quotes the Energy Ministry reporting fires and temporary operational halts. Reuters via CNA reports satellite smoke observations but says ground images and witnesses were unavailable. The casualty figure remains attributed to Saudi authorities, not independently established here.
latest_news.implication: Reported fires and temporary operational halts affect southern Saudi energy facilities; the casualty total remains attributed.

latest_news.headline: AFP revises Umm Rawaba strike toll from 12 to 13 dead; 22 injured
latest_news.text: AFP reports a hospital source revised the death toll from 12 to 13 after another person died of injuries; 22 injured remain in treatment. RSF responsibility remains attributed, with no immediate RSF comment. This updates the same September 8 strike outside the courthouse, not a separate attack.
sources: AFP via France 24; earlier AFP via Arab News (same agency, not independent confirmation)
latest_news.implication: The same courthouse-area attack has a revised reported casualty toll; responsibility remains attributed.

latest_news.headline: UK commits GBP100 million to Ukraine winter air defence
latest_news.text: UK Ministry of Defence confirms a GBP100 million PURL contribution including Patriot missiles, with delivery planned before winter. This is military assistance, not a collective-defence invocation.

latest_news.headline: New Hintalo strike allegation warrants close watch
latest_news.text: AFP reports a TPLF allegation of a September 8 drone strike; a hospital source reports at least three wounded. AFP could not independently verify the claim, and the federal army had not commented. No confirmed death toll or new activation.

latest_news.headline: AFP reports deadly strike outside Umm Rawaba courthouse
latest_news.text: A medical source tells AFP 12 people were killed; witnesses describe a drone striking a tree outside the courthouse. RSF responsibility remains attributed and there was no immediate RSF comment. Do not infer confirmed destruction of the courthouse.

latest_news.headline: Destroyer commissioning adds nuclear-posture concern
latest_news.text: Dong-A reports KCNA announced September 6 commissioning of Kang Gun Ho and Kim nuclear-navy remarks. This does not establish actual warhead loading, a new launch or a nuclear explosion. Canonical test flags remain unchanged.

latest_news.headline: Zaporizhzhia power reconnection gains IAEA-attributed corroboration
latest_news.text: Interfax-Ukraine attributes September 7 Ferosplavna-1 reconnection to Energoatom and an IAEA statement following locally protected repairs. This improves nuclear safety without establishing a general cessation of hostilities.

latest_news.headline: Saudi energy fires corroborated; existing signal retained
latest_news.text: Reuters reports Saudi energy-facility fires and a coalition account of 73 wounded across four southern cities on September 8. Coalition warns of an operational response. Existing facility-attack signal is not counted twice.

latest_news.headline: Zaporizhzhia grid restoration: stronger sourcing, residual risk
latest_news.text: Hromadske full September 8 report attributes September 7 restoration of Ferosplavna-1 power to Energoatom. This improves verification beyond prior index-only coverage but is not a directly verified new IAEA restoration statement. New Kyiv strikes reported; localized nuclear-safety repairs do not imply general ceasefire.

latest_news.headline: Iran repeats exclusion-zone threats; operational extent unverified
latest_news.text: September 8 Reuters via Geo reports renewed economic-warfare and exclusion-zone threats. Missile use is an Iranian claim referring to prior days; US denies hits. No verified zero traffic or fresh minefield. Historical mining flag retained, not freshly corroborated.

latest_news.headline: Inspection gap persists; UN referral still a draft
latest_news.text: September 8 Al Jazeera/Reuters confirms continuing IAEA information/access gap; E3/US referral resolution remains unsubmitted draft. No new weapons-grade enrichment or test verified.

latest_news.headline: Saudi energy disruption keeps oil risk elevated
latest_news.text: Saudi-attributed disruption remains an existing signal, not a new activation. Reuters syndication quotes Brent $99.00 and WTI $94.41 at 08:00 UTC; timestamped intraday prices, not live quotes.

latest_news.headline: Saudi energy sites hit; operational stoppages reported
latest_news.text: September 8 Al Jazeera full direct report quotes Saudi energy ministry: energy sites hit early Tuesday, fires and temporary operational halts. Houthis subsequently claim a large missile/drone operation. AP also reports Saudi-attributed 73 wounded; Al Jazeera says the coalition did not date that casualty total. Activate infrastructure_strike; do not imply independently audited damage or confirmed territorial gains. Existing score remains saturated.

latest_news.headline: Newer reports say Zaporizhzhia external power restored
latest_news.text: September 7 evening Ukrainska Pravda, Energoatom-attributed coverage and an IAEA-attributed headline report restored external electricity. This supersedes an unqualified repairs-pending narrative, but remains index-level in this run; official IAEA feed carries earlier statements and direct statement access is challenged. Grid reliability remains a watch item; retain existing localized repair-arrangement signal.

latest_news.headline: Iran referral still a draft; verification gap persists
latest_news.text: September 8 Al Jazeera/Reuters reiterates Iran material-accounting and on-site verification gaps; the E3/US referral draft is not yet formally submitted in that report. No new technical threshold independently established; keep existing access-gap signal.

latest_news.headline: Iran threatens Gulf energy assets; restricted zone proposed
latest_news.text: Reuters September 7 full extract confirms conditional Gulf energy threats and a proposed restricted zone; neither establishes zero traffic or a freshly verified minefield. Retain historical mining status with explicit verification caveat; no score increase.

latest_news.headline: Freedom Edge confirmed; destroyer report is prior context
latest_news.text: September 6 destroyer commissioning remains prior context; September 7-11 Freedom Edge confirmed by DVIDS. Neither establishes a new configured DPRK test this scan; hold.

event_forecast.explanation: Numeric event predictions are withheld until event definitions, time horizons, resolution rules and independent validation gates pass. Withheld means unknown, not zero risk. Inherited signal scores are not calibrated event probabilities.

source_limitations: Source coverage and corroboration have not been independently verified for this build. Official releases are preferred for attributable actions; reputable reporting may add context. Headline indexes, repeated reports and market prices are not independent confirmation. Missing or stale reports do not establish calm. Single-source claims remain unverified.
